summary: Lamb Weston EMEA (legal entity Lamb Weston B.V.) makes frozen fries, potato specialties and dried potato flakes for foodservice, retail and the food industry. It has offices in Breda and Kruiningen in the Netherlands and six factories in the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and Austria. It began as a 1994 joint venture of Meijer Frozen Food and Lamb Weston.
founded: 1994 (joint venture of Meijer Frozen Food, 1985, and Lamb Weston, 1950)
products: Potato specialties (twisters, crisscuts, dippers, wedges, hash browns, rösti)
Frozen potato products for supermarket retail
Dried potato flakes for the food industry
Semi-finished products for soups, mash and binding
markets: Products sold in more than 110 countries
Sales offices in São Paulo (Brazil) and Lagos (Nigeria)
facts: Produces more than 30,000 tonnes of potato flakes a year
Meijer family began growing potatoes in Kruiningen in 1920
Meijer Frozen Food began frozen products and flakes in 1985
Acquired four plants (Oosterbierum, Bergen op Zoom, Wisbech, Hollabrunn) in 2000–2010
limitations: Current ownership of the European business and the terms of the 1994 joint venture are not stated on the pages read.
